Label: Solo Effects

Label: Clear
Notes: Emergency Clear (plan 2.2, 4.4-10). Long-press flushes this channel's chain, feed delay lines and return ring; Ctrl = all channels. Not a stored parameter. R4-10: it memsets one delay line per source and may drop a block or two.

Label: Loop Guard LED
Notes: Read-only. Lit while this channel's loop guard has ramped its fx-to-fx feed bus to -inf (plan 4.4-9, corrected by R4-1/R4-2). Not a control.
Hover help text in the status bar: The loop guard has muted this channel's effect-to-effect feed.

Label: Cycle Warning Badge
Notes: Read-only. Raised on the message thread when this channel sits inside a cycle of the effect-to-effect on-switch graph (plan 2.2). No audio-side action: the user owns the loops.
Hover help text in the status bar: This effect is part of a feedback loop in the sends grid.

Label: Re-layout Effects
Notes: Long-press. Re-runs the automatic ring placement over every effects channel and clears effectPositionsUserOwned on <Effects>. Decision 15 / Q9: effects never share the input/reverb position latch.
Hover help text in the status bar: Long-press to lay every effect return out on the default ring again.

Label: Selected Effect
Notes: Max bounded by the Effects Channels count in System Config (up to 32). Display channel name on the switches. No identifier is declared for it: the selection is GUI state. The sibling files do NOT leave this cell blank - WFS-UI_reverb.csv names reverbSelected (and input/output theirs) on the selector row and tool_generation_ignores.json drops all three as "UI-only selection state, no ValueTree backing". A blank cell reaches the same tool surface without an ignore entry; name it here only if an effectSelected identifier is ever declared.
Hover help text in the status bar: Effects Channel Number and Selection.
Keyboard shortcuts: Type E to switch to the Effects Tab. Prompt in the status bar for 5 seconds to type a number and then return to select the corresponding effects channel.

Label: Link Group
enum: Unlinked (0) ; Group 1 (1) ; Group 2 (2) ; Group 3 (3) ; Group 4 (4) ; Group 5 (5) ; Group 6 (6) ; Group 7 (7) ; Group 8 (8)
Notes: Node <Channel>. Each channel is in at most one group. Module parameters, module bypasses and chain order propagate; feeds, position, otomo and name never do. Group names come from effectsGlobalLinkNames; the absolute/relative behaviour from effectsGlobalLinkMode.
Hover help text in the status bar: Link this effect to a group so module edits propagate to the other members.

Label: Link Mode
Notes: Node <Channel>. The MODE is per channel, the exact mirror of outputApplyToArray; effectsGlobalLinkMode is only the value a NEW channel is stamped with. Propagation consults the RECEIVER's mode as well as the origin's, so a member set to Off is skipped whichever channel the edit is made from - that is what "disengage temporarily" means. Leaving the group (effectLinkGroup = 0) is "disengage permanently"; Relative is "conserve relative offsets", and applies to continuous values only.
Hover help text in the status bar: How this channel takes group edits: off, absolute, or relative.

Label: Mute
Notes: Node <Channel>. R4-8: mute silences the feed entering the chain and lets the chain keep running - it must not skip the sweep, or every tail would freeze. PREFIX COLLISION: effectMute is a strict prefix of effectMutes, effectMuteMacro and effectMuteReverbSends.

Notes: Node <Channel>. Transient: applied as a mask in the calculation engine, never on the audio thread. Plan 7.3 lists it for tool_generation_ignores.json, so it is expected to be declared here and skipped by the generator.

The name starts with "effect", so it needs a BY-NAME exception ahead of getParameterScope's prefix test - without it the prefix test routes the write into the Effect branch, finds no channel node, and drops it in silence. Input-to-effect feeds are never touched.
Hover help text in the status bar: Automatically mute an effect-to-effect feed that is running away.

Label: Loop Guard Ceiling
Notes: Config > EffectsGlobal, a child of <Config> and NOT a sibling of the <Effect> channels. The name starts with "effect", so it needs a BY-NAME exception ahead of getParameterScope's prefix test - without it the prefix test routes the write into the Effect branch, finds no channel node, and drops it in silence. Peak ceiling, in dBFS. R4-2: the trip threshold is a TIME (default 60 ms), not a block count, so the same event does not let eight times as much runaway through at a 512 sample buffer as at 64.
Hover help text in the status bar: Peak level at which the loop guard trips (dBFS).

Label: Maximum Delay Time
Notes: Config > EffectsGlobal, a child of <Config> and NOT a sibling of the <Effect> channels. The name starts with "effect", so it needs a BY-NAME exception ahead of getParameterScope's prefix test - without it the prefix test routes the write into the Effect branch, finds no channel node, and drops it in silence. Sizes EVERY delay module's buffer: nextPow2(seconds x sr + maxBlock), about 2-4 MB per channel at the 5 s default and 15-31 MB at 20 s. A stopped-engine setting, and the ceiling of effectDelayTime / effectDelayTapTime.
Hover help text in the status bar: Longest delay any effects channel may buffer, in seconds.

Label: Feed Compute Device
Notes: Config > EffectsGlobal, a child of <Config> and NOT a sibling of the <Effect> channels. The name starts with "effect", so it needs a BY-NAME exception ahead of getParameterScope's prefix test - without it the prefix test routes the write into the Effect branch, finds no channel node, and drops it in silence. Compute device id for the feed stage ("cpu", "hip:0", "cuda:0", ...). The engine is CPU-only in v1; this is the hook for the optional later feed-on-GPU phase.
Hover help text in the status bar: Compute device used for the effects feed stage.

Label: Effects Channels
Notes: Config > IO property, next to reverbChannels. A CONFIG property despite the "effect" prefix, so it needs a by-name Config exception ahead of the prefix test. Locked when DSP is running. Reducing the count prompts a confirmation before removing channel settings. Max is maxEffectChannels, asserted against spatcore::effects::kMaxEffectChannels.
Hover help text in the status bar: Number of Effects Channels.
